author: Soraya Kishtwari
title: Zuckerberg’s $300m Yacht Reportedly Ignored Call for Help From Stranded Boat
content:
A superyacht owned by Mark Zuckerberg failed to come to the assistance of a small boat that called for help near Alaska last week.

The 21ft motorboat issued a general request for assistance after it ran out of fuel between Petersburg and Juneau on 3 August.

A small cruise ship that was further away than Zuckerberg’s yacht ended up helping the boat after picking up the call from the coastguard,

Zuckerberg was not on board at the time. His spokesperson said the superyacht didn’t hear the call for help in time because it was using a different radio channel.

A passenger travelling on the Wilderness Legacy, which rescued the boat, said there was “unanimous booing” on board when the captain announced that the billionaire’s $300m 387ft yacht had failed to answer the call for help – despite its proximity to the boat. “Our boat rescued a stranded vessel last night and apparently we did that after the Coast Guard radioed Mark Zuckerberg’s yacht – which was closer – and they repeatedly refused to respond. (There was near unanimous booing when the captain announced this),” Michael Love wrote on Bluesky. “Frankly, if I was Mark Zuckerberg I would be absolutely ecstatic at a chance to do something helpful for someone in need and maybe get some good PR out of it.”

A spokesperson for Zuckerberg denied the accusations. In an email to the Alaskan Beacon, which initially reported the inciden

author: Novara Media
title: Ex-Oil Engineer Turned Climate Whistleblower: We Face Collapse.
content:
The summer of 2026 will go down in history books as the hottest, driest and most deadly set of heatwaves Britain has ever experienced. This weather isn’t normal – but it is predictable according to a global consensus of scientists. And yet this summer, according to the science, will be one of the coolest summers we ever have again. Things will only get hotter from here.

Beginning his career as an oil-rig engineer before retraining as a climate scientist, Kevin Anderson’s career has been an extraordinary journey. On Downstream this week, Aaron Bastani sat down with him to discuss what has become his life’s work: sounding the alarm on man-made climate change, and on the fossil fuel industry that gave him his start.

Just how much has the planet heated, and why? Is the Paris Agreement’s aim of keeping heating to beneath 1.5°C still achievable, or delusional cope? What are the political obstacles to tackling the issue? Having worked with Andy Burnham in Manchester, what does Kevin think he will do on climate, as PM? Is avoiding catastrophe still possible, and if so, how much time have we got to act, before it’s too late?

author: Novara Media
title: Why Do British Seaside Towns Vote Reform?
content:
Despite the cold winds, sewage spills and ouch-y pebbles, British people love the beach. But if the beach was that good, surely we wouldn’t have needed to invent claw machines?

In this episode, Nadia, Keir and Jem compare their emotional connections to the seaside – from Southport sands to the Red Sea – and think about why humans are drawn to the border between water and land.

They also talk about the beach in deep-time, the birth of surf culture and why seaside towns vote Reform, with music from 808 State and The B-52’s. Sous les pavés, la plage!

Follow our Spotify playlist of all the music discussed on ACFM and subscribe to the ACFM mailing list to get weirder and leftier.

author: Soraya Kishtwari
title: BBC Axed Report on British Army Killing Unarmed Child in Derry
content:
The UK government successfully lobbied the BBC to axe a report revealing the British Army killed an unarmed child in Derry during the Troubles in 1972, newly released documents reveal. A week after 15-year-old Daniel Hegarty was shot dead, the Ministry of Defence falsely claimed he had been killed from a distance of 25 metres by a soldier who believed the child was armed. But a memo sent days after the 31 July incident showed senior personnel knew Hegarty had in fact been killed by a “general purpose machine gun” at point-blank range. Hegarty’s killer was an 18-year-old known only as ‘Soldier B’, who shot him during Operation Motorman, a British Army push to retake “no-go areas” controlled by residents and Irish republican paramilitaries. Soldier B reportedly told an October 1973 inquest: “I cocked the weapon and when the youths were about 25 metres away I aimed at the leading man and fired a quick burst” of bullets. The declassified documents, obtained by the Pat Finucane Centre, show that BBC Panorama correspondent Alan Hart spoke to witnesses of the shooting who said Hegarty and two cousins who were with him were unarmed and posed no threat.

Hart then approached the British Army in Derry for comment. His request reached the office of prime minister Edward Heath, whose press secretary Donald Maitland instructed a senior official at the Northern Ireland Office (NIO) to “persu

author: Soraya Kishtwari
title: EU Moves to Share Data With Israel That ‘Could Be Used to Kill Palestinians’
content:
The EU is pushing ahead with a controversial data-sharing agreement with Israel despite warnings that it could enable the targeting and killing of Palestinians, an investigation by the NGO Statewatch has found.

Under the plans, the bloc’s law enforcement agency, Europol, would exchange sensitive personal information about Palestinians with Israel’s police force, which is headquartered in the illegally occupied West Bank.

There is also concern the deal could harm members of the  Palestinian diaspora, with a risk that activists in Europe could be targeted.

The data would include names, identification numbers, locations, genetic and biometric information and details about people’s political views, beliefs and personal lives.

Since 2005, the EU has run a mission in the West Bank to support the Palestinian Authority with policing. Rights activists have previously warned that the data sharing deal could turn members of this civilian mission into “informants” for Israel.

In a recently leaked 2022 document obtained by Statewatch, the EU Council’s legal advisors warned that allowing data to be used in the occupied Palestinian territories risked legitimising Israel’s occupation, in breach of international law.

But negotiations have continued despite this advice. The bloc’s executive branch, the European Commission, held meetings on the deal with Israeli officials between 2023 and 2

author: Novara Media
title: The Age of the West Is OVER. Here’s Why.
content:
In the years since October 7th, the world has been bitterly polarised over how to make sense of the violence. While polling shows that a majority of people do believe Israel’s actions amount to genocide – having witnessed it with their own eyes via their smartphones – it has been woefully hard to find mainstream media outlets in the West prepared to use this language.

On Downstream this week, Aaron Bastani sat down with Indian essayist and novelist Pankaj Mishra. His most recent book, ‘The World After Gaza’ takes stock of a world order shattered by the genocide, and a media class unprepared to recognise the truth. In response to these crises, Mishra and colleagues have just launched Equator magazine, pulling together leading writers from across the globe who are unafraid to tell the truth.

When did the so-called West first begin to lose standing in the eyes of the rest of the world? Why is the British media class positioned so uniquely close to power, so delusional, and so compromised over Gaza? Will China replace America, in the coming century, as the new hegemonic power? Has it already?

author: Simon Childs
title: Boy George Releases Reggae Song Denying Israel’s Genocide
content:
Boy George has released a pro-Israel reggae song with lyrics that deny a genocide is happening in Palestine.




The song, entitled “Od Nikrod (We Will Dance Again)”, was posted on the Culture Club frontman’s X account along with the comment “#Shalom”.




The lyrics say: “You say genocide, I say war. When you’re attacked, it’s what the army is for. Does it get ugly? You bet it does. When I know you want to kill every last one of us.”




The phrase We Will Dance Again is a reference to the 7 October Hamas attack on the Supernova Sukkot Gathering festival which led to the death of 378 people.




The song also criticises the pro-Palestine movement saying: “You condemn the Jews, with selective memory. Musicians holding flags, mouthing like sheep. Propaganda fuelled by the internet feels so weak.”




The song was panned by users of X with one calling it a “depraved piece of repellant Zionist propaganda”. Even the pro-Israel Telegraph newspaper admitted it “might not be his best” but said it “is his bravest”, complimenting its “rootsy and authentic Jamaican reggae feel.”




The song appears to be a stepping up of support for Israel from Boy George. Previously, he said he did not have an opinion on the country.

author: Simon Childs
title: Hospitals See ‘No Notable Improvement’ After Using Palantir Tool
content:
Hospitals noticed “no notable improvement” after using a patient discharge tool from Palantir, a US tech company with ties to the US and Israeli militaries.




NHS trusts that use the tool found “no meaningful difference” in discharge delays, according to analysis by the Health Foundation, a think-tank.




The findings contrast with claims from NHS England that using the Federated Data Platform causes a 15% fall in long-stay discharge delays. Palantir won a £330m contract to build the platform in 2023.




An NHS England analysis seen by the Financial Times was restricted to long-stay discharges because the tool was “mainly designed to support the management of complex patients”.




Critics told the newspaper that this analysis was flawed.




Steve Black, a healthcare consultant and former NHS data scientist, said: “It is dangerous to selectively quote evidence like that because its success should be judged against fixing the underlying problem, which is how do we better manage all discharges to free up more beds.”




Palantir said the Health Foundation report “appears to misunderstand what the tool does”.




In June, MPs called for the government to trigger a break clause in the contract and find a UK-based provider.

title: Israeli Settlers and Soldiers Launch Fresh Wave of Pogroms in West Bank
content:
Israeli forces and settlers have intensified their attacks against Palestinians in the illegally occupied West Bank in recent days, killing and injuring several people, demolishing homes and setting fire to mosques.




​

The escalating violence began on Thursday, when settlers and soldiers killed four Palestinians and injured eight across the West Bank. 




On Friday, a group of armed settlers attacked Palestinians on their land in the village of Tal, killing at least four people. During the incident, a Palestinian man seized an attacker’s weapon and shot and killed two Israelis.




Walid Zidan, the mayor of Tal, said some 20 settlers attacked the village at around 8am. “Residents rushed to defend homeowners in the area,” he said,

 

according to Drop Site News

.




Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu and defence minister Israel Katz responded to the deaths of the two Israelis by ordering weapons raids, the demolition of homes and the revocation of work permits for Palestinians in certain villages.  




​

“The security forces must be allowed to operate freely and with full force,” the two leaders said.

author: Novara Media
title: Who Profits From Genocide?
content:
A new consensus has emerged in Westminster, seemingly overnight: we need more defence spending, and we need it now. But the Ministry of Defence has a record for waste that would put Tony Soprano to shame. £13 billion down the drain, since 2010, at the very least. Aircraft carriers that come in late, overbudget, and beset by mechanical failures. IT systems that cost millions, and are wildly out of date. No other government department could get away with it. But the arms trade spends billions of dollars on greasing the wheels of political consent. They employ armies of lobbyists, print reams of analysis, and bribe politicians the world over to keep the war machine funded. The result isn’t just a crisis of corruption. It’s a threat to our survival as a species.




Andrew Feinstein is a former-minister in the South African government, turned investigative reporter. He is the executive director of Shadow World Investigations, and serves on the board of Declassified UK. And in 2024, he stood against Keir Starmer in Holborn and St Pancras. He joins Ash Sarkar on Downstream to lift the lid on how the arms industry really works, and tell us about his political journey.

author: Novara Media
title: What JD Vance and Tucker Carlson Actually Believe
content:
The American empire is in crisis – and there is a new generation of more vocal critics coming from the right.




So what do JD Vance and Tucker Carlson actually believe about American power?




James Pogue has reported on empires and their decline for years, from West and Central Africa, where Wagner Group picked over the corpse of French neo-colonialism, to California’s secessionist fringe and the absurdities of Washington.




He also happens to be one of the closest observers of JD Vance, who is just a heartbeat from one of the most powerful positions in the world.




The president’s real job is keeping the machine running: asset prices up, markets juiced, the war economy fed. Can anyone actually change that? And would we even want them to try, if it’s as ideologically peculiar and dangerous as Vance?

author: Sophia Sheera
title: Met Police U-Turns on Decision Not to Investigate Brits Who Served in IDF
content:
The Metropolitan police has U-turned on its decision not to investigate Brits who served with the Israel Defense Forces (IDF) over alleged war crimes in Gaza. 




The Met’s war crimes team received a landmark 240-page dossier of evidence in April 2025, submitted by legal experts on behalf of the Palestinian Centre for Human Rights (PCHR) and the Public Interest Law Centre (PILC).




The dossier alleged that ten British nationals – including dual citizens – had committed war crimes and crimes against humanity while fighting with the IDF in Gaza, including “wilful killing, extermination, attacking civilians, and deportation or forcible transfer of population”. 




A year later, Novara Media revealed that the Met had decided not to open an investigation. This was despite more than 70 legal and human rights experts urging the police to take action in accordance with international law.




The Met has now backtracked after British-Palestinian human rights campaigner Lubna Speitan, who is represented by the PILC, threatened judicial review proceedings against the force.




Following the possibility of a legal challenge, the Met confirmed it will open a “fresh scoping exercise” in relation to four of the ten British nationals. 




Scoping exercises are undertaken by the Met’s war crimes team to decide whether to conduct a full investigation.

title: Gary Lineker Joins 100+ Millionaires Asking Andy Burnham to Tax Them More
content:
More than 100 UK-based millionaires including Gary Lineker, screenwriter Richard Curtis and city trader turned wealth tax campaigner Gary Stevenson are asking Andy Burnham to tax their wealth and “reinvest” it into Britain. 




“We want you to tax us,” reads their letter, organised by Patriotic Millionaires UK and delivered on Thursday. “We’re not talking about higher taxes on those who get up and go to work for their income every day, but on the very richest whose income is derived from the wealth they hold.”




Polling from Patriotic Millionaires shows that 80% of UK millionaires 

support a 2% tax on wealth over £10m, which the group says would raise 

£24bn a year for Britain. 




Patriotic Millionaires also advocates for reforms to capital gains tax, including equalising it with income tax, to raise an estimated £12bn annually. 




Other signatories to the letter include musician Brian Eno, novelist Val McDermid and lawyer Julia Davies. 




Lineker said: “Paying your fair share is a basic British value, but so many ordinary people are already paying more than they can afford. Our richest people can do more and most want to.”




Burnham has not ruled out introducing a wealth tax, and has previously suggested he would consider an inheritance tax levy on estates to fund social care.

author: Joshua Carroll
title: Former Southern Water Boss Charged With Conspiracy to Defraud
content:
Former Southern Water CEO Matthew Wright has been charged with conspiracy to defraud, as have three other former employees.




Wright and his co-defendants are alleged to have conspired to defraud the Environment Agency (EA) and Ofwat by cheating water quality tests between 1 January 2012 and 31 December 2017.




They are alleged to have manipulated a compliance testing regime known as Operator Self-Monitoring (OSM), which requires water companies to take samples at wastewater treatment centres and report the results to the EA.  




The four are accused of conspiring to “defraud persons performing public duties in respect of environmental and financial regulation” using “the implementation of artificial no-flow events at waste water treatment works”.




At the time, OSM rules said samples did not have to be provided if the discharge flow was insufficient to take one. 




The EA last year requested a summons against Wright, along with Philip Barker, Clive Massey and Mark Gregory, but Wright tried to block the move at the High Court, where his lawyers argued the EA did not have the power to issue a summons.  




That argument was dismissed on Wednesday, bringing an end to reporting restrictions on the case.

author: Joshua Carroll
title: Burnham Lets Trump Use British Bases for Illegal War on Iran
content:
Andy Burnham has granted US president Donald Trump permission to use British military bases as part of his illegal war on Iran.




The 

new prime minister

 made the call after being briefed on a high-level meeting about British policy on the war that happened before he took office, 

Bloomberg reported

.




It means the US military will be able to use Diego Garcia in the Indian Ocean and RAF Fairford in Gloucestershire to conduct bombing runs. The US renewed its attacks on Iran on 8 July.




More than 3,468 people have been killed by US and Israeli attacks on Iran since 28 February, including more than 121 children and 26 teachers in a massacre by the US at a school in Minab.




​After entering Number 10 on Monday, Burnham spoke to Trump on the phone. “The prime minister outlined the UK’s commitment to securing the movement of shipping in the Strait of Hormuz,” Burnham’s office said in a statement.




​Like his predecessor, Keir Starmer, Burnham’s office claims the UK’s bases will only be used for “defensive” strikes, despite the fact the US-led war has no basis in international law and is unprovoked.​




Trump has made no secret of the fact the US is attacking civilian targets in Iran, including bridges, oil refineries and power plants. In April he warned Iran that “a whole civilisation will die tonight”, raising fears that he was prepared to use nuclear weapons.

author: Simon Childs
title: US Creates ‘Blacklist’ of Prominent Leftwing Politicians and Groups
content:
Prominent leftwing politicians, influencers and groups have been named in a US department of state report into Cuba’s “sustained campaign of subversion” against the US.




New York City mayor Zohran Mamdani, streamer Hasan Piker, Democracy Now host Amy Goodman and Ben and Jerry’s founder Ben Cohen, are among those named in the 100 page report entitled “Cuba: The Capital of 21st Century Communism” which was released on Monday.




The report, described by journalist Ken Klippenstein as a “blacklist”, also lists the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA), a major grassroots group that canvasses for and endorses leftwing politicians.




Presenting little if any evidence for its claims, the report says Cuba has conducted “a campaign that has infiltrated the highest reaches of the US government, recruited and cultivated generations of American activists, backed an unprecedented wave of leftwing terrorism on American soil, and carried out one of the most durable and damaging foreign intelligence penetrations in American history.”




Promoting the report on X, secretary of state Marco Rubio wrote: “For more than six decades, the Cuban regime has been the leading sponsor of radical leftism and Third Worldism in the United States.”

title: Britain ‘Does Not Have Enough Water’ for Planned AI Data Centre Boom
content:
The UK faces water shortages because government forecasts do not take into account the expansion of data centres, water companies have said.




The government has “all but forgotten that most data centres require water to cool their systems”, according to a briefing to MPs from Water UK, a trade body representing water companies. 




The briefing suggested weakening environmental protections so that more water can be drawn from the environment to expand the AI sector.




The government’s forecasts for water usage “explicitly exclude” data centres, the briefing said. The stinging critique said the government’s data centre plans said official forecasts are “fatally flawed”.




Meanwhile, three government plans – the department for Science, Innovation and Technology “Delivering AI Growth Zones” plan, the AI for Science Strategy and the AI Opportunities Action Plan – all fail to mention water, the briefing said.




“There appears to be an assumption that the country will always have enough water for its economic needs. Nothing could be further from the truth,” it said.




Water UK used its briefing to propose reducing limits on water abstraction in water-stressed parts of the country. “Water companies could have these caps suspended temporarily, to allow them to enable data centre and other growth, while they develop new water supply options,” the briefing said.

author: Novara Media
title: You Will Rent Forever. Here’s Why.
content:
We live in times of crisis. But perhaps none of the crises affect so many people in the here and now, as the housing crisis. Solving it could provide the skeleton key to unlocking so many of society’s problems. Despite this, decades of successive governments in the UK have failed to bring housing under control. The social contract which told us that if we worked hard all our lives, we can own a home and be secure in retirement, has been completely broken.




To discuss the crisis in Britain and beyond, Aaron Bastani sat down with Peter Apps. He is an award-winning journalist who knows the field of housing – its failures and its potential fixes – better than almost anyone. He wrote an article about the threat of flammable cladding a month before Grenfell caught fire.




How has housing policy shaped Britian in the last 50 years? Who did more to damage the housing system, Labour or the Tories? Is more housing supply always the solution? And why is no one talking about the crisis facing our ageing population, one million of whom will be in housing insecurity and poverty by 2030?

title: An Israeli Property Fair Is Still Advertising Illegal West Bank Homes to Brits
content:
An Israeli property roadshow is still advertising homes in illegal West Bank settlements to prospective buyers in the UK – even after London mayor Sadiq Khan 

raised the matter 

with the Metropolitan police, the Home Office and the Foreign Office.  




Organisers of the ‘Great Israeli Real Estate Event’ 

apologised last month

The event’s organisers claimed West Bank settlements had been included “by mistake”. But organisers have since contacted mailing list subscribers with an email promoting the sale of more West Bank homes on behalf of Israeli real estate company Harey Zahav. 




The 2 July email, seen by Novara Media, offers “affordable private houses in Anglo communities”. It advertises “20+ projects in prime locations, close to the centre of the country and to Jerusalem”. It says all projects are located in “Judea and Samaria”, the name the Israeli government gives to the West Bank. 




Israeli settlements in the West Bank are built in occupied Palestinian territory and considered illegal under international law.

reported by DeSmog

Farage is currently facing a self-triggered byelection after being investigated for failing to disclose a £5m donation from crypto billionaire Christopher Harborne. The MP for Clacton has also been scrutinised for his ties to George Cottrell, a convicted fraudster, who the Times revealed this week

made undisclosed donations to Reform

.

CPAC Great Britain is modelled on the annual gathering of conservative thinkers and politicians in the United States. Jacob Rees-Mogg, historian David Starkey, former Tory leader Iain Duncan Smith, and Israel’s deputy foreign minister Sharren Haskel are scheduled to appear at the event.

author: Joe Sandler Clarke
title: British Troops Dropped Prisoners From Forklift ‘For Fun’, Afghanistan Inquiry Hears
content:
British soldiers dropped Afghan prisoners from a forklift “for fun”, an inquiry has heard.

The Afghanistan inquiry is investigating alleged war crimes by UK special forces from 2010 to 2013 – as well as claims of a cover-up.

Whistleblowers Monica Grenfell and Christopher Green decided to give evidence after a request for witnesses to come forward was made by inquiry chairman Lord Justice Haddon-Cave.

Grenfell, who worked as a mess hand, or kitchen worker, with the SAS at that time, said she had met a soldier who told her about prisoners being abused.

“I specifically recall him telling me that he would put prisoners on a forklift, raise it up and drive very fast so that they fell off,” she said.

Green, who served in Afghanistan between January and September 2012, told the inquiry he was dismissed as a “Taliban-loving apologist” after raising concerns about the killing of three Afghan farmers by the SAS.

He said his own unit’s intelligence team believed there was “nothing to suggest” the men were Taliban commanders. Still an SAS representative insisted they were and that the men had drawn weapons when engaged. Green asked to see footage of the SAS raid to fact check this, but was denied.

The mother of the three farmers was then paid the equivalent of £3,634 in cash by the UK government, money that was described as an “assistance payment”, the inquiry heard.

author: Novara Media
title: Shabana Mahmood Set to Be Chancellor

author: Joshua Carroll
title: Meta Used AI to Target Disabled and Pregnant Workers for Layoffs, Lawsuit Claims
content:
Dozens of workers are suing Meta over claims it used AI to identify workers for mass layoffs, with those taking disability or maternity leave disproportionately targeted.

The lawsuit, filed in California on Monday on behalf of 26 employees, alleges that a “constellation of internal artificial intelligence systems” was used to sack people by looking at their keystroke and activity monitoring data.

“Meta did not assemble the termination list through the considered judgment of managers who knew the work,” it reads.

The lawsuit points to the company’s recent layoff of 8,000 workers, and alleges that Meta used AI to assess workers’ productivity but did not take into account time off for medical reasons or because they were due to give birth.

“The result was that employees who took protected leaves were disproportionately selected for layoff, based on scoring that not only failed to account for their protected leaves, but in effect penalised the employees for exercising their legal rights to these leaves,” the complaint said.

One of the plaintiffs was told she was being laid off just two days before she gave birth, despite the fact she had been approved for pre-birth pregnancy leave. Another is an engineer who received a “lowered rating” because he took time off for an injury.

A Meta spokesperson told the Guardian the claims in the lawsuit “lack merit and are not based on fact,

author: Joshua Carroll
title: Green-Led London Council Plans to Block ‘ICE-Style Immigration Raids’
content:
Green party-led Lewisham council is planning to ban cooperation with the Home Office on ‘ICE-style’ immigration raids.

Councillors will vote next Wednesday on a motion to conduct a review “with the explicit aim of refusing to assist immigration enforcement wherever legally possible”, the party said in a statement.

The review would examine data-sharing and service agreements to ensure there is a “firewall” between council services and immigration enforcement. It will also look at any contracts the council has with groups helping to facilitate raids.

The homelessness charity St Mungo’s may be included in the review after it was found to have shared information with the Home Office about migrant rough sleepers in 2019, the Guardian reported.

The motion would also commit the council to supporting the Lewisham Anti-Raids network “by helping migrant businesses and people targeted by raids understand their legal rights… and ultimately prevent and resist raids,” the Green party said.

“ICE-style immigration raids tear people away from their families, their neighbours and their communities and have no place in a decent society,” Green party leader Zack Polanski said.

author: Joshua Carroll
title: Colombia’s Outgoing President Says Israeli Firm Meddled in Election
content:
Colombia’s outgoing president, Gustavo Petro, has accused an Israeli cyber intelligence company of meddling in the country’s recent election, in which a far-right, pro-Israel candidate beat his leftwing rival by a margin of less than 1%.

The firm, BlackCore, allegedly waged a disinformation campaign against both Petro and his ally Ivan Cepeda, who was running for the presidency against the US and Israel’s preferred candidate, Abelardo de la Espriella.

“BlackCore, the Israeli company, deployed 500,000 bots – fake profiles – to manipulate the Colombian electorate with millions of lies about Ivan and me,” Petro wrote on X last week.

De la Espriella secured 49.66% of the vote in a run-off election on 21 June, narrowly beating Cepeda’s 48.7%. At the time, Petro alleged that foreign actors had accessed the website of Colombia’s National Registry and manipulated polling data.

“The only entity in the world capable of doing that is the state of Israel,” he said. Colombia’s attorney general Gregorio Eljach dismissed the allegations and said there was “no evidence of fraud”.

Petro is among Israel’s fiercest critics on the world stage. In 2024 he broke diplomatic ties with the country “for having a government, for having a president who is genocidal”.

author: Harriet Williamson
title: Israel Is Holding the Bodies of Palestinians As ‘Bargaining Chips’
content:
Israel is holding the bodies of over 100 Palestinians who have died in its custody since October 2023 as “future bargaining chips”, a new report by Tel Aviv-based human rights group Gisha has found.

At least 68 of the 104 Palestinians who died or were killed in Israeli detention are from Gaza.

As well as being unable to bury their loved ones, bereaved families are also denied accurate information about how they died.

Withholding corpses is considered a form of collective punishment against Palestinians and a violation of international law by legal experts and rights groups.

Israel has previously claimed it was holding Palestinian bodies for the purpose of hostage negotiations. However, there are no Israeli captives remaining in the Gaza Strip.

Gisha’s 8 July report,

Abuse of the Dead

, details a case where Israel admitted it was holding onto a detainee’s body until a new policy is made regarding hostages and missing persons.

Gisha states: “The authorities effectively acknowledge that they are holding bodies as bargaining chips” – a move that “lacks legal basis and constitutes arbitrary punishment of bereaved families”.

Israel is currently detaining over 9,000 Palestinians on what it defines as “security” grounds – the majority from the West Bank and Gaza – as of July 2026. Approximately

author: Simon Childs
title: Man on Trial for Helping Iranian Spy Worked for the Telegraph, Court Told
content:
A man accused of helping an Iranian spy in his high-profile prison escape attempt worked for the Telegraph newspaper, a court has been told.

Imran Chowdhury, 26, from Chingford, east London, is accused of assisting Daniel Khalife, who went on the run after escaping HMP Wandsworth on 6 September 2023 while awaiting trial for spying for Iran. Chowdhury is being tried at Snaresbrook crown court alongside Adeel Khan, 32, from Waltham Forest. Both deny the charges.

Khalife sparked a police manhunt after hiding underneath a food delivery van as it left the prison grounds. He was recaptured three days later and sentenced in 2024 to 14 years and three months for spying for Iran.

On Tuesday, Thomas Williams KC, speaking for the prosecution, told the court that around the time Khalife was making his escape attempt, Chowdhury “was at work at the offices of the Telegraph newspaper where he worked in a technical role – not a journalist, it’s important we’re clear about that.”

He told the court: “You may conclude that his job meant, for instance, that he had a good understanding of digital technology,” and that due to his role in a news organisation Chowdhury had full knowledge of who Khalife was.

Williams said the event was “the highest profile escape from prison in many years, given that he [Khalife] was a soldier charged with espionage and terrorism offences.”

author: Harriet Williamson
title: Trump Administration Announces Plan to ‘Dismantle’ the ICC
content:
The US state department has launched a plan to “disable” and “dismantle” the International Criminal Court (ICC), which includes pressuring other countries to join in and threatening to cut US assistance for those that don’t.

President Donald Trump’s administration has opposed the ICC’s attempts to investigate Israeli war crimes in Gaza and US war crimes in Afghanistan, despite welcoming its investigation into Russian war crimes in Ukraine.

US secretary of state Marco Rubio announced a “whole-of-government campaign” against the court on Monday, accusing it of “waging a war against our country, not with bullets or missiles,” but with “the force of so-called international law”.

In a video message posted to X, Rubio said: “If they believe they can deprive us of our sovereignty, we will teach them the full meaning of American resolve.”

The ICC can only investigate crimes committed in states that are party to the Rome statute – which includes Palestine. The US and Israel are among 29 states that are not.

A state department official told CNN: “Nations that refuse to reject the ICC’s false authority while relying on US assistance are likely to come under increased scrutiny.” Possible punishments for countries that don’t comply could include sanctions, travel bans and revoked visas.

author: Harriet Williamson
title: Andy Burnham Votes for Labour’s Draconian Immigration Crackdown
content:
Andy Burnham, Britain’s next prime minister, voted in favour of home secretary Shabana Mahmood’s 

authoritarian immigration bill

 last night.




He did so even after more than 80 Labour backbenchers wrote to warn him that the party is “losing progressive voters” due to Mahmood’s authoritarian stance.




The bill means successful asylum seekers, once they start earning, will be charged up to £10k for any 

accommodation

 and financial support they received while waiting for their claims to be processed. People awaiting a decision on their asylum claim in the UK are generally not allowed to work, meaning they have little choice but to accept state help. 




Rights groups have condemned the policy as an “extra tax on refugees” fleeing war, torture and persecution. Child asylum seekers whose claims aren’t resolved until after they turn 18 will also be liable. 




The immigration and asylum bill passed its second reading in the House of Commons with 264 votes to 90 on Monday evening, with 14 Labour MPs rebelling.




The new legislation will make it easier for the government to deport people seeking asylum in the UK by tightening the application of Article 8 of the European Convention on Human Rights – which protects the right to private and family life – in order to make it more difficult to appeal asylum decisions.

author: Novara Media
title: The Middle Class Will Collapse Unless We Tax the Rich
content:
The idea of a wealth tax has never been more popular in Britain, and while many have campaigned for it, none have done more to boost the demand than one man: Gary Stevenson. 




The former city trader first joined us on Downstream four years ago. A lot has changed since then. This week, after a bruising round of media including attacks from Piers Morgan and the Guardian, Gary sat down to give his side of the story to Novara Media’s Aaron Bastani. 




What are the fair critiques of a wealth tax, and how does Gary engage with them? Why does Gary claim the British middle class is facing collapse? What would he say to Andy Burnham? What does he think needs to be done, to keep out Farage and Reform? And do the recent spate of attacks in the media show that – counter to what they say – Gary’s actually winning the argument?
